proposals.evidence: CDIAL 6152 danta gives Gujarati/Marathi/Hindi dā̃t tooth. The printed source has dental d/t, matching this family. Visual inspection of PDF physical p. 34 confirms dental-stop glyphs misread as ɖ/ʈ by the stored source ledger. This link follows the printed reading, not an invented retroflex sound change. Stored form ḍaṭ and its durable ID are preserved pending a separately audited source correction. Final -e variants are retained in the same lexical family, without assigning an unsupported grammatical category.
